pillar_reactions.evidence: The most specifically targeted pillar delivery in the batch — the rep named the prospect's own pathology back to him before making any claim: 'remember when you said that you had the elbow surgery, the EDS, the shoulder dislocation, tightness with your hip flexors, which also is connected to lower back pain, knee pain, everything is connected, and that's why kettlebell workouts are way different, because in every session you work as a unit.' He then tied the benefit to the prospect's actual life rather than a generic outcome: 'when you get stronger, you're going to be showing up to work better. You can hold up the frame on the door and not being injured after that.' Reaction was minimal — 'Yes, sir' and 'Right' — hence accepted rather than enthusiastic. Recorded alongside it, because it matters more than the reaction: the pillar was presented as the remedy for symptoms caused by a genetic connective tissue disorder, and no one asked whether the prospect's chiropractor or physical therapist would sanction loaded ballistic work for hypermobility.

Delivered with good personalisation on one axis and a blind spot on another. The rep addressed the sweet tooth directly and warmly ('Mr. Sweet Tooth'), pre-empted the objection that dieting is punishing ('it's not about making your life harder... no extreme dieting, no obsessive tracking, no weighing on a scale'), gave the standard three variables, and adapted it to a long working day: 'if you have longer days that you need to eat out or whatever, you're going to know what to do.' The prospect said 'Sounds good' and nothing more. The blind spot is the constraint he had already disclosed thirty-two minutes earlier: 'At the moment, money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper.' A prescription of whole foods, eggs, meat, chicken, vegetables and fruit is more expensive than what he currently eats, and the cost of it was never mentioned. For this prospect the nutrition pillar has a price attached that the offer never acknowledges.

Well positioned against his documented history — 'you told me that you've tried some things, but you didn't stick to it, with the chiropractor and the exercises that you got from the physiotherapist' — and explicitly tied back to the self-sabotage work done earlier: 'this is going to be very important, because we're going to cover the devil on your shoulder.' The in-pillar reaction was flat, an 'Okay'. Scored accepted on that basis. But this is the pillar the prospect had already bought, twelve minutes before it was presented and in his own words, when asked why this attempt would be different: 'having somebody that's keeping me accountable is a huge step in the right direction.' He had also granted the rep a personal accountability mandate — 'do I have your permission to hold you accountable, to hold you to the fire?' / 'Yeah.' Of the three pillars this is the one that had genuine, volunteered demand behind it, and it is the one he could not pay for.

anchors.raw: Only about 40, $40 cash on hand... that's just what's for gas. I have groceries that I have scheduled out. So my mortgage is paid and my loans are paid.
anchors.note: The most extreme affordability position in the corpus, and the reason this call is a clean loss rather than a negotiation. Forty dollars is not a low balance, it is the residue after fixed costs, earmarked for fuel. No payment plan, financing partner or discount reaches this position. The rep established it in two questions and correctly stopped.

anchors.raw: Currently paying back my retirement for an issue that I had in the house. And I've got my mortgage. So there's not much wiggle room. And the retirement will be paid off in two years. And then I've got the credit card. So I don't have a specific time for it.
anchors.competitor: A retirement-account repayment, a mortgage on a recently bought house with problems, and a credit card being paid down
anchors.note: A stack of prior claims with a two-year horizon on the nearest one and no defined end on the furthest. This is what converts the objection from a timing problem into a disqualification: there is no near date at which the picture changes, and the prospect said so himself.

anchors.raw: At the moment, money's a little tight, so there is more carbs than I should be, just because it's cheaper.
anchors.note: The earliest financial signal on the call, at 00:07:39, and the most diagnostic one — a prospect whose grocery composition is dictated by cost was never going to fund $6,000. It was also a direct warning about the nutrition pillar that would be delivered thirty-two minutes later, and it was not picked up either time.

anchors.raw: I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time. I can't do either of them.
anchors.note: Second occurrence in this batch of an ad-sourced prospect meeting the price cold, after Jorge Fernández. This one arrived not knowing who Trevor was — asked how well he knew the work, he said 'not at all actually' — and reached minute forty-seven with no price band in mind. The apology is worth noting on its own: a prospect who feels guilty for wasting a closer's time is a prospect the funnel should never have routed to a closer.

anchors.raw: I did get Trevor's free follow along guide. And once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all. I have no problems with doing a little bit here and there.
anchors.note: The free-alternative anchor appears here in its least damaging form — the prospect is not using it to argue against the price, he is using it as a stopgap until he can afford the real thing, and he volunteered the distinction himself. The rep's response was the right one commercially and personally: he endorsed the plan and extended it, promising to send further materials, which converts a dead deal into a nurture relationship at no cost. Worth recording as the one instance in this batch where the free product worked in Primal's favour at the point of loss.

anchors.raw: I would say motivation, but also, I'm just tired, man. I get up at 3, home by 2, and then...
anchors.note: Recorded deliberately as a null result. There is no supportive anchor anywhere on this call: no history of paying for coaching, no partner or family member mentioned at any point, no prior premium purchase in any category, no referral, and no discretionary spending of any kind disclosed. The only paid interventions in his history — massage therapy and chiropractic — both ended, one because the therapist moved and one because it stopped working. Across this batch, the complete absence of a supportive anchor has tracked the outcome more reliably than any single objection.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded ballistic kettlebell training is appropriate for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome — a genetic connective tissue disorder producing recurrent joint subluxation, in a prospect who dislocated a shoulder catching a door and whose kneecap subluxes when he walks.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no clinical screening step in the process and no mechanism to consult the clinicians already treating him. This is the one call in the batch where the rep did ask whether doctors were involved and whether prescribed exercises were being followed, which makes the omission sharper rather than softer: he had a chiropractor and a physical therapist named on the call and never asked whether either would sanction the training, then presented that training as the fix for exactly those symptoms. Whether the programme helps or harms someone with hypermobility is genuinely unknown to everyone who was on this call, and it should be answered by a human before any similar prospect is sold to.

unmet_demand.want: A nutrition approach that works on a constrained grocery budget — he eats more carbohydrate than he wants specifically because it is cheaper, and schedules his groceries.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The pillar prescribes whole foods, eggs, meat, chicken, vegetables and fruit, which costs more than what he currently eats, and cost is not addressed anywhere in it. Primal could presumably build budget-aware guidance — this is a formatting and content gap rather than a capability limit — but at present the nutrition system implicitly assumes food spend is not the binding constraint. Given that this is also the batch's clearest affordability disqualification, it is worth noting that the same assumption runs through the offer and the pillar alike.

unmet_demand.want: Something between the free follow-along guide and $6,000 for a prospect with real need, real intent and no money — he proposed the interim path himself and asked to come back when his debts clear.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing exists between the free guide he already has and the six-month programme. The rep improvised the only available answer, promising to send further free materials and to stay in touch, which is the right instinct and is not a product. Third occurrence of this gap in this batch, after Jorge Fernández's used-bicycle analogy and Jared Lyons's request to buy a programme rather than a relationship — three prospects in four sales calls asking for a rung on the ladder that does not exist, for three entirely different reasons.

unmet_demand.want: A way to train around an extreme schedule and genuine exhaustion — up at 3am, out by 5, physical work until 2.30pm, then a 30 to 50 minute drive home.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Recorded as served rather than as a gap, and included so the rollup does not misread this loss. The 30-to-40-minute at-home format answers this want directly, the rep made that point explicitly ('you don't have to commute anywhere, you can do it in your garage'), and the prospect accepted it. What was never addressed is the sleep debt underneath the exhaustion, which was never asked about and which no amount of programme design fixes.
